biases.debias: Report specific criticisms of institutional performance without suggesting the institution itself lacks purpose.
biases.example_text: As Israel pushes past the Litani, Lebanese question the purpose of UNIFIL
biases.unbiased_text: As Israel pushes past the Litani, Lebanese debate UNIFIL's effectiveness

biases.detail: Framing infrastructure achievements as unconvincing through public doubt assertions despite successful completion.
biases.debias: Report infrastructure completion and adoption rates separately from opinion polling on satisfaction.
biases.example_text: Egypt's new monorail offers a modern ride, but Cairo is still not convinced
biases.unbiased_text: Egypt's new monorail opens to passengers, with initial ridership data still being collected

biases.detail: Framing US involvement in foreign separatist movements through questioning rather than assertion creates conspiratorial atmosphere without making direct claims.
biases.debias: Report confirmed facts about separatist movements and international involvement without speculative connection questions.
biases.example_text: Alberta will vote in a referendum over whether to separate from Canada, but how is the US President involved?
biases.unbiased_text: Alberta will vote in a referendum over whether to separate from Canada. The US President has commented on Alberta's autonomy discussions.

biases.detail: Emphasizing removal of identity documents to frame medical evacuation as imprisonment rather than administrative processing.
biases.debias: Report medical evacuation logistics neutrally, distinguishing between security measures and deliberate detention.
biases.example_text: Palestinian patients stripped of their documents are confined inside a Baghdad medical centre.
biases.unbiased_text: Palestinian patients evacuated to Baghdad are awaiting document processing at a medical centre.

biases.detail: Tallying foreign leader visits as evidence of growing influence frames diplomacy as competitive achievement rather than routine engagement.
biases.debias: Report diplomatic visits as part of standard international relations without competitive tallying.
biases.example_text: China has hosted 26 leaders from 23 countries this year, underscoring its growing diplomatic and economic influence.
biases.unbiased_text: China has hosted 26 leaders from 23 countries this year as part of ongoing diplomatic engagement.

biases.detail: Using 'Doesn't seem qualified' in headline format to delegitimize appointees through rhetorical questioning rather than direct assertion.
biases.debias: State qualifications objectively based on verifiable credentials and relevant experience without framing through subjective questioning.
biases.example_text: 'Doesn't seem qualified': Who is Bill Pulte, acting US intelligence chief?
biases.unbiased_text: Bill Pulte appointed acting US intelligence chief: Background and qualifications

biases.detail: Using phrases like 'won't be allowed to embed' to presume hostile intent in visa decisions without direct evidence of such framing by authorities.
biases.debias: Report visa restrictions and stated rationales without inserting terminology that assumes covert operational intent.
biases.example_text: Squad's visas for the US haven't been issued, with Marco Rubio saying IRGC-linked members won't be allowed to 'embed'.
biases.unbiased_text: Squad's visas for the US haven't been issued, with Marco Rubio stating that individuals linked to the IRGC will not receive entry approval.

biases.detail: Treating animal-based event predictions as newsworthy content rather than entertainment trivializes sports coverage.
biases.debias: Exclude or clearly label animal prediction segments as entertainment novelty rather than presenting them as sports news.
biases.example_text: Shark predicts winning start for Brazil at FIFA World Cup.
biases.unbiased_text: A shark at an aquarium was part of a promotional event related to Brazil's World Cup match.

biases.detail: Elevating protests against foreign health facilities without substantiating underlying conspiracy-adjacent concerns frames legitimate disease preparedness as suspicious.
biases.debias: Clarify the scientific purpose of health facilities while reporting objections, avoiding amplification of unverified threat narratives.
biases.example_text: The plan has drawn backlash from  Kenyans as well as the country's union of healthcare workers.
biases.unbiased_text: Some Kenyans and healthcare workers have raised concerns about the facility, though the US maintains it is for disease surveillance and preparedness.

biases.detail: Questioning whether ceasefires exist through headline interrogatives while simultaneously reporting violations, implying the agreements are meaningless rather than merely breached.
biases.debias: Report ceasefire agreements as formal accords while documenting specific violations, without questioning the existence of the agreements themselves.
biases.example_text: Gaza, Iran, Lebanon: If ceasefires are in place, why do strikes continue?
biases.unbiased_text: Gaza, Iran, Lebanon: Strikes continue despite ceasefires

biases.detail: Elevating fan opposition to managerial appointments into newsworthy political crises based solely on prior national team coaching roles.
biases.debias: Report fan reactions as community sentiment without framing routine supporter disagreements as political controversies deserving international coverage.
biases.example_text: Celtic fans oppose Keane as potential manager after Israel role
biases.unbiased_text: Celtic fans divided on potential Keane appointment as manager

biases.detail: Framing routine visa application procedures as newsworthy diplomatic events requiring urgent international attention and resolution.
biases.debias: Report visa processing as standard administrative procedures without suggesting they represent extraordinary diplomatic hurdles or crises.
biases.example_text: Iran footballers hand passports to US embassy for World Cup visa approval
biases.unbiased_text: Iran footballers apply for US visas ahead of World Cup

biases.detail: Emphasizing the temporal proximity between a victim's anticipated joyful event and their death to maximize emotional impact and victimization narrative. Also: Amplifies emotional impact by highlighting the minimal time gap between a victim organizing an event and their death, emphasizing cruel timing coincidence.
biases.debias: Report deaths factually without emphasizing the timing relative to planned celebrations or personal milestones. Report the death and the planned event separately without emphasizing temporal proximity for emotional effect.
biases.example_text: Muhannad Farwana never got to wear his wedding suit, Israel killed him in an air strike hours before his wedding.
biases.unbiased_text: Muhannad Farwana was killed in an Israeli air strike on the day he was scheduled to be married.

biases.detail: Treating satirical protest movements with unconventional names as legitimate political entities through neutral coverage that normalizes their framing.
biases.debias: Clarify the satirical or protest nature of movements with symbolic names while reporting their actual political demands.
biases.example_text: 'Cockroach Party' leader returns to India for first New Delhi protest.
biases.unbiased_text: Leader of satirical youth protest movement using 'Cockroach Party' branding returns to India for first New Delhi demonstration.

biases.detail: Framing routine visa processing delays or denials as deliberate diplomatic crises or discrimination campaigns.
biases.debias: Report visa issues as administrative matters unless there is clear evidence of discriminatory policy.
biases.example_text: Iranian officials say a 'large' number of key staff denied visas as the team is set to travel to Mexico.
biases.unbiased_text: Iranian officials said some staff members have not yet received US visas ahead of the team's World Cup participation.

biases.pattern: War economic impact household cost individualization
biases.detail: Translating geopolitical conflict into personalized household financial burden through precise dollar amounts to emphasize individual victimization.
biases.debias: Report economic impacts through aggregate indicators and market data without converting to individual household cost figures that personalize distant conflicts.
biases.example_text: On average, US households have spent $750 more in expenses due to the war, hitting middle and lower-income people hard.
biases.unbiased_text: The war has contributed to rising energy and commodity prices in the United States, affecting consumer costs.

biases.pattern: World Cup logistical policy reversal vindication
biases.detail: Framing FIFA's policy change on water bottles as a victory resulting from public backlash and official criticism rather than routine operational adjustment.
biases.debias: Report policy changes as administrative updates without constructing narratives of grassroots triumph over institutional decisions.
biases.example_text: New York Mayor Mamdani was among those critical of FIFA's decision to ban water bottles at World Cup stadiums.
biases.unbiased_text: FIFA reversed its water bottle policy at World Cup stadiums following feedback from officials and the public.

biases.detail: Elevating routine visa processing decisions into international diplomatic incidents that suggest deliberate political exclusion.
biases.debias: Report visa denials as administrative matters without inferring broader diplomatic significance unless officials explicitly frame them as such.
biases.example_text: Iran's ambassador to Mexico expressed concern over the reported denial of US visas to the World Cup delegation.
biases.unbiased_text: Iran's ambassador to Mexico said some World Cup delegation members did not receive US visas.

biases.detail: Using informal diminutive names (like 'baby Sam') instead of formal names in headlines to heighten emotional impact and victimization framing of Palestinian casualties.
biases.debias: Use the child's full formal name as provided by family members or official sources without diminutive terms.
biases.example_text: 'Lives turned in a second': Family of baby Sam, shot dead by Israel, grieve
biases.unbiased_text: 'Lives turned in a second': Family of seven-month-old shot dead by Israel grieves

biases.detail: Framing sports tournament climate conditions as a broader political or social crisis requiring expert warnings rather than standard venue planning considerations.
biases.debias: Present climate conditions as logistical considerations for the event without elevating them to crisis-level warnings.
biases.example_text: Climate experts warn that 25% of World Cup games could be played in very hot conditions, affecting fans and players.
biases.unbiased_text: Analysis shows that 25% of World Cup games will be played in hot conditions, with organizers preparing heat management protocols for fans and players.

biases.detail: Attributing political leader's responses to psychological vulnerability ('thin skin') rather than strategic calculation.
biases.debias: Describe the political response factually without psychological speculation about emotional sensitivity.
biases.example_text: A student parody account has rattled India's most powerful man and exposed just how thin his skin has become.
biases.unbiased_text: A student parody account has prompted a response from India's prime minister, raising questions about the government's approach to online criticism.

biases.detail: Emphasizing the unprecedented geographic spread of opening ceremonies as historically significant.
biases.debias: Report the multi-country hosting arrangement without elevating it to historic status.
biases.example_text: The 2026 World Cup begins with historic ceremonies across the US, Canada and Mexico, launching a record tournament.
biases.unbiased_text: The 2026 World Cup begins with opening ceremonies across the US, Canada and Mexico for the expanded tournament.

biases.detail: Using passive voice to obscure key details about perpetrators or victims while emphasizing certain aspects of an incident.
biases.debias: Use active voice construction and include all relevant identifying information available in balanced manner.
biases.example_text: US State Department confirms the fatality, but refuses to provide more information about the person's death in Yangon.
biases.unbiased_text: The US State Department confirmed a US diplomat died in Yangon and said a Thai woman is in custody, but declined to provide additional details about the death.

biases.detail: Framing sanctions or diplomatic measures as insufficient without providing objective criteria for adequacy.
biases.debias: Report on sanctions and their scope without editorial judgment on whether they meet unstated standards of sufficiency.
biases.example_text: Sanctions on settlers not enough: Target Israeli gov't, say campaigners
biases.unbiased_text: Campaigners call for sanctions to extend beyond individual settlers to include Israeli government officials

biases.detail: Describing a military UFC event at the White House as occurring 'in front of Donald Trump' frames the president as merely a spectator prop rather than event organizer or host.
biases.debias: Describe the president's role at events with neutral framing that acknowledges their organizational authority without editorializing.
biases.example_text: Fight time, undercard, stats and how to watch as Topuria and Gaethje tussle in front of Donald Trump at the White House.
biases.unbiased_text: Fight time, undercard, stats and how to watch as Topuria and Gaethje compete at the White House-hosted UFC event.

biases.detail: Framing a comedian's work as a survival mechanism through their cultural identity during conflict, elevating entertainment to existential necessity.
biases.debias: Report on comedians' work and career without framing their comedy as a survival strategy or existential response to geopolitical events.
biases.example_text: He's become one of the most prominent Palestinian voices in comedy, but can Mo Amer laugh through this moment?
biases.unbiased_text: Mo Amer has become one of the most prominent Palestinian voices in comedy, continuing to perform and create new material.

biases.detail: Presenting archaeological findings of female-led societies as newsworthy discoveries that validate contemporary gender politics.
biases.debias: Report archaeological findings based on their scholarly significance without framing them as validation of contemporary social movements.
biases.example_text: Archaeologists have discovered evidence of an ancient female-led society in the ruins of a city in present-day Turkiye.
biases.unbiased_text: Archaeologists have discovered evidence of social structures in the ruins of an ancient city in present-day Turkiye, with researchers analyzing patterns of governance and authority distribution.

biases.detail: Treating AI model predictions of sporting outcomes as legitimate forecasting worthy of news coverage, validating speculative technology.
biases.debias: Avoid treating AI-generated predictions as newsworthy content; report on actual outcomes and expert analysis instead.
biases.example_text: We asked four AI models to predict the winner of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
biases.unbiased_text: The 2026 FIFA World Cup has begun, with sports analysts offering various predictions based on team performance, player fitness, and tournament history.

biases.detail: Amplifying social media backlash against celebrity statements on Palestine to construct narrative of widespread condemnation.
biases.debias: Report celebrity statements and measure actual response magnitude rather than amplifying selective backlash as representative.
biases.example_text: US actor Jerry Seinfeld is facing backlash after saying Palestine 'doesn't exist'.
biases.unbiased_text: US actor Jerry Seinfeld said Palestine 'doesn't exist' in a recent interview, generating responses on social media.

biases.detail: Framing dangerous substitute products as established alternatives rather than crisis-driven health hazards, normalizing life-threatening behaviors through neutral terminology.
biases.debias: Emphasize the health risks and crisis conditions forcing these dangerous substitutions rather than presenting them as viable alternatives.
biases.example_text: Smokers in Gaza turn to toxic molokhia nicotine cigarettes as tobacco prices surge, causing serious health risks.
biases.unbiased_text: Desperate smokers in Gaza are poisoning themselves with makeshift molokhia cigarettes after tobacco became unaffordable, exposing them to severe health risks.

biases.detail: Presenting theft of sports equipment as potentially meaningful sabotage through headline framing rather than as routine crime, implying targeted disruption without evidence.
biases.debias: Report equipment thefts as criminal incidents without implying coordinated targeting unless evidence supports such conclusions.
biases.example_text: England training equipment stolen ahead of squad's arrival in Kansas City
biases.unbiased_text: Training equipment bound for England's World Cup squad was stolen in Kansas City, local police confirmed.

biases.detail: Presenting technology export controls as barring foreigners from access rather than as national security measures, framing them as discriminatory restrictions.
biases.debias: Describe export controls neutrally as regulatory measures without presuming discriminatory intent or framing access as an entitlement.
biases.example_text: Foreigners barred from accessing top AI models, underscoring Donald Trump's policy of export controls over high tech.
biases.unbiased_text: The US government has directed Anthropic to restrict access to its most advanced AI models as part of export control policies.

biases.detail: Highlighting removal of political figure's name from institutions as newsworthy achievement rather than routine administrative action.
biases.debias: Report name changes as administrative updates without celebratory or vindictive framing unless there is broader significance.
biases.example_text: Trump's name has been removed from the Kennedy Center after a court ruling, but adorns many other things and places.
biases.unbiased_text: A court ruling resulted in the removal of Trump's name from the Kennedy Center; his name remains on other properties and venues.

biases.detail: Framing current allegations as part of a longstanding pattern to suggest systematic institutional behavior rather than isolated incidents.
biases.debias: Report allegations based on current evidence without presuming systematic historical patterns unless comprehensively documented.
biases.example_text: Sexual violence against Palestinians in Israeli custody is often framed as a post-October 7 issue. But historical record
biases.unbiased_text: Reports of sexual violence against Palestinians in Israeli custody have emerged, with some analysts examining whether similar allegations have occurred historically.

biases.detail: Describing a deal as simultaneously 'complete' and requiring further signing ceremonies, creating confusion about its actual status while projecting momentum.
biases.debias: Clarify the precise stage of negotiations by distinguishing between preliminary agreements, signed documents, and implementation timelines.
biases.example_text: The Deal with the Islamic Republic of Iran is now complete
biases.unbiased_text: The US and Iran have reached a preliminary agreement, with formal signing scheduled for Friday.

biases.detail: Presenting one party's claim that multiple issues are necessarily connected as established fact rather than a negotiating position.
biases.debias: Attribute linkage claims to specific parties and note that different actors may view issue connections differently.
biases.example_text: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson says ending the war in Lebanon is an 'inseparable' part of the US-Iran agreement.
biases.unbiased_text: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson stated that, from Tehran's perspective, ending the war in Lebanon should be included in the US-Iran agreement.

biases.detail: Foregrounding the specific young age of child casualties in headlines to maximize emotional impact and frame incidents as particularly egregious.
biases.debias: Report child casualties with factual age information in context without using age as the primary emotional framing device in headlines.
biases.example_text: Israeli forces kill three-year-old Palestinian boy on family farm in Gaza
biases.unbiased_text: Israeli forces killed a Palestinian child and wounded his father on a farm in Gaza, according to family members.

biases.detail: Emphasizing location details that favor one narrative while omitting geographic proximity that would reveal logistical coordination challenges.
biases.debias: Include all relevant geographic details that affect operational feasibility without selective omission.
biases.example_text: US visa rules leave Senegal's World Cup fans behind
biases.unbiased_text: Senegalese fans face visa processing challenges for World Cup matches in North America

biases.detail: Characterizing standard operational decisions or logistical challenges as deliberate oppression or persecution.
biases.debias: Describe logistical decisions as operational matters without imputing systematic persecution motives.
biases.example_text: Iran coach says team 'oppressed' by travel chaos after World Cup NZ draw
biases.unbiased_text: Iran coach criticizes travel logistics after team forced to relocate between matches

biases.detail: Presenting contradictory qualities of a leader side-by-side without clarifying context, creating confusion about intent or meaning.
biases.debias: Provide the full context of remarks to clarify whether contradictory characterizations are complimentary, critical, or contextually dependent.
biases.example_text: President Donald Trump praised Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a "killer" and an "angel" at the G7 in France.
biases.unbiased_text: President Donald Trump made remarks about Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the G7 in France, calling him both a "killer" in negotiations and an "angel" in diplomatic relations.

biases.detail: Amplifying accusations of bribery regarding diplomatic agreements without explaining the nature of negotiated incentives or settlements.
biases.debias: Distinguish between negotiated incentives in diplomacy and corrupt bribery, providing proper context for what agreements entailed.
biases.example_text: US President Donald Trump has accused his predecessor Barack Obama of 'bribing' Iran to agree to the 2015 nuclear deal.
biases.unbiased_text: US President Donald Trump criticized his predecessor Barack Obama's approach to the 2015 nuclear deal, characterizing the economic sanctions relief as improper inducement to Iran.

biases.detail: Pre-labeling a political candidate with ideological terms in headlines before describing their positions or qualifications.
biases.debias: Describe candidates' positions and qualifications before applying ideological labels, allowing readers to form their own assessments.
biases.example_text: US progressive Lewis George on track to become DC mayor after Trump threats
biases.unbiased_text: US Democrat Lewis George on track to become DC mayor after Trump threats

biases.detail: Framing an athlete's inability to travel as being 'unauthorised' due to an arrest, implying legal restriction rather than administrative process.
biases.debias: Clarify whether travel restrictions are legal requirements or administrative decisions by sports authorities.
biases.example_text: Wahi was unauthorised for travel after he was reportedly arrested last month in a French spot-fixing investigation.
biases.unbiased_text: Wahi was denied entry to Canada after he was reportedly arrested last month in a French spot-fixing investigation.

biases.detail: Emphasizing victim nationality in headlines before context to maximize emotional impact and regional identification.
biases.debias: Present incident context before nationality markers to avoid emotional manipulation through identity framing.
biases.example_text: Three killed in Ukraine a day after drone attack kills child in Moscow
biases.unbiased_text: Casualties continue in conflict with three killed in Ukraine and one child killed in Moscow drone attack

biases.detail: Connecting professional body sanctions to unproven allegations through headline juxtaposition suggesting guilt.
biases.debias: Separate factual professional actions from ongoing investigations without implicit causation links.
biases.example_text: British lawyers' body suspends ICC Prosecutor Khan over misconduct claim
biases.unbiased_text: ICC Prosecutor Khan suspended by British bar association during ongoing misconduct investigation

biases.detail: Highlighting unfamiliarity with a location to amplify unexpected political importance and reader intrigue.
biases.debias: Present geographic context neutrally without emphasizing reader ignorance for dramatic effect.
biases.example_text: Ashton-in-Makerfield, a town few knew of until recently, has potentially chosen the UK's next prime minister.
biases.unbiased_text: Ashton-in-Makerfield by-election results may influence UK leadership succession

biases.detail: Framing climate change as uniquely threatening a specific religious minority's ancient traditions and homeland, emphasizing existential cultural endangerment.
biases.debias: Report climate impacts on highland communities without foregrounding religious identity as the primary vulnerability frame.
biases.example_text: In Lubra, Nepal's last Bon village, climate-driven floods are destroying homes and land, endangering ancient traditions.
biases.unbiased_text: In Lubra, a highland village in Nepal, climate-driven floods are destroying homes and land, threatening the community's way of life.

biases.detail: Framing foreign corporate involvement in domestic resource projects as inherently detrimental to national interests without presenting counterarguments.
biases.debias: Present multiple perspectives on foreign investment in renewable energy, including economic benefits and sovereignty concerns.
biases.example_text: Giving concessions for renewable projects to foreign corporations will not help solve the country's energy crisis.
biases.unbiased_text: Critics argue that renewable energy concessions to foreign corporations may not address Tunisia's energy crisis, while supporters cite needed investment and expertise.

biases.detail: Emphasizing symbolic reenactments of historical atrocities to elevate contemporary political demands, creating moral urgency through theatrical representation.
biases.debias: Report on reparations conferences and their substantive proposals without foregrounding dramatic reenactments as the primary framing device.
biases.example_text: Slave trade reenacted on Juneteenth as leaders demand reparations
biases.unbiased_text: Leaders mark Juneteenth by demanding reparations at conference addressing slavery's legacy

biases.detail: Framing the creation of commercial sports leagues as fundamentally transforming lives and revolutionizing a field, emphasizing glamour and social change.
biases.debias: Report on women's sports development with specific participation and economic data rather than sweeping transformation claims.
biases.example_text: In cricket-obsessed India, a women's World Cup win and a glitzy new league are transforming the lives of female players.
biases.unbiased_text: India's women's cricket has grown following a World Cup win and the launch of a new professional league, increasing opportunities for female players.

biases.detail: Framing a political candidate's statements about foreign policy through the lens of their rivalry with the current leader rather than the policy itself.
biases.debias: Report foreign policy statements on their own merits without emphasizing internal political competition.
biases.example_text: An old clip has resurfaced showing Andy Burnham saying Israel would be his first overseas visit if elected as UK PM.
biases.unbiased_text: A video shows Andy Burnham previously stating that Israel would be his first overseas visit if elected as UK Prime Minister.

biases.detail: Framing a competitor's suspension as directly benefiting another athlete through title gap reduction emphasis.
biases.debias: Report sports results without attributing success to competitors' absences or penalties.
biases.example_text: Seven-time MotoGP world champion reduces title leader Marco Bezzecchi's points lead after the Italian was suspended.
biases.unbiased_text: Seven-time MotoGP world champion Marc Marquez won the Czech MotoGP, reducing the points lead of championship leader Marco Bezzecchi.

biases.detail: Framing inflation rates or events through time-based superlatives to amplify crisis perception without contextualizing magnitude or comparison.
biases.debias: Report inflation figures with historical context and comparative benchmarks rather than chronological superlatives alone.
biases.example_text: Canada's inflation hits 29-month high amid heightened oil prices
biases.unbiased_text: Canada's inflation rate increased to 3.2% in May, driven primarily by oil prices

biases.detail: Attributing mundane infrastructure issues to political sabotage by named opponents to manufacture controversy.
biases.debias: Report infrastructure maintenance issues factually without attributing political motives unless substantiated by investigation.
biases.example_text: Donald Trump, who spent $14m relining the iconic pool, claims it has been vandalised by 'radical left lunatics'.
biases.unbiased_text: Donald Trump, who spent $14m relining the iconic pool, has claimed vandalism, though officials cite algae growth as the cause.

biases.pattern: Gaza World Cup heroism isolation framing
biases.detail: Presenting Gaza's sports infrastructure collapse as unique abandonment story to emphasize victimization through FIFA inaction.
biases.debias: Report sports infrastructure challenges factually with concrete details about FIFA commitments and implementation status.
biases.example_text: Gaza's footballers train on broken pitches with no shoes. Why has FIFA's rebuilding plan gone nowhere?
biases.unbiased_text: Gaza's football infrastructure remains damaged, with FIFA's 2024 rebuilding commitment yet to be implemented.

biases.detail: Referring to leaders by first name only in headline to suggest informality, lack of authority, or diminished stature.
biases.debias: Use full names or standard titles for political figures consistently regardless of position on issues.
biases.example_text: Why has Keir Starmer resigned as UK prime minister, and who will take over?
biases.unbiased_text: Why has UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer resigned, and who will take over?

biases.detail: Framing the revelation that Israel smuggled communication technology into Iran as a casual admission rather than an illegal intelligence operation.
biases.debias: Report technology smuggling operations as intelligence activities with legal and diplomatic implications rather than matter-of-fact admissions.
biases.example_text: Former PM Naftali Bennett has admitted Israel smuggled Starlink internet systems into Iran.
biases.unbiased_text: Former PM Naftali Bennett revealed that Israel conducted covert operations to introduce Starlink internet systems into Iran.

biases.detail: Transforming routine national team selection into celebratory milestone narrative through emphasis on jersey presentation ceremony.
biases.debias: Report athlete selections as standard sporting news without ceremonial emphasis unless the selection itself is historically unprecedented.
biases.example_text: Teenage star receives first India shirt from BCCI and is tipped to make his debut in a T20 match in Ireland on Friday.
biases.unbiased_text: Teenage player Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has been selected for India's T20 squad and is expected to debut in Ireland on Friday.

biases.detail: Characterizing US health facility funding as masking risks rather than as partnership with stated public health objectives.
biases.debias: Report international health facility projects through stated objectives and documented concerns rather than assumed hidden motives.
biases.example_text: Kenya stops constructing US-run Ebola site amid public outcry; $13.5m US funding is criticised as masking health risks.
biases.unbiased_text: Kenya halted construction of a US-funded Ebola facility following public concerns and a court order; critics questioned the $13.5m project's necessity.

biases.detail: Framing Iranian public sentiment with contradictory 'cautiously optimistic' language that simultaneously validates hope while emphasizing doubt and complexity ahead.
biases.debias: Report public sentiment directly without hedging contradictions; separate optimism from concerns factually.
biases.example_text: Iranians cautiously optimistic about thorny deal with US
biases.unbiased_text: Iranians express mixed views on US deal as months of negotiations lie ahead

biases.detail: Highlighting unusual temperature patterns where traditionally cooler European cities exceed Middle Eastern temperatures to amplify climate crisis narrative.
biases.debias: Report actual temperatures and their impacts without comparative surprise framing across distant regions.
biases.example_text: When Paris is hotter than Mecca: How Europe's heatwave compares globally
biases.unbiased_text: Paris temperatures exceed 40C as Europe experiences severe heatwave

biases.detail: Elevating conflicting claims about unfrozen funds' use to create impression of diplomatic chaos or deception.
biases.debias: Report the substantive disagreement factually without framing either side's position as definitive or contradictory revelation.
biases.example_text: The denial contradicts the US administration, which said unfrozen funds will be spent on produce from American farmers.
biases.unbiased_text: Iran's negotiator said unfrozen funds would not be spent on US goods, while the US administration has stated the funds will be used to purchase produce from American farmers.

biases.pattern: Diaspora fear juxtaposition with sporting pride
biases.detail: Pairing celebratory sports coverage with fear narratives about the diaspora community to inject political anxiety into cultural achievement.
biases.debias: Cover sporting achievements and community concerns as separate topics without combining them to suggest celebration is overshadowed by fear.
biases.example_text: For Haitians in the US, the pride and joy of the World Cup comes with fear
biases.unbiased_text: Haitian diaspora communities in the US celebrate their team's World Cup participation after a 52-year absence from the tournament.

biases.detail: Platforming pro-Brexit voices with phrases like 'no regrets' to validate controversial decision while minimizing opposing perspectives.
biases.debias: Present Brexit anniversary coverage with balanced representation of various voter perspectives and documented outcomes rather than selective vindication.
biases.example_text: 'We did regain control': The Brexit voters with no regrets 10 years on
biases.unbiased_text: Ten years after the Brexit vote, some UK voters say leaving the EU was the right decision, while polling data shows mixed public sentiment on the outcome.

biases.detail: Framing high turnover of political leaders as systemic pathology unique to specific country rather than comparative political phenomenon.
biases.debias: Report leadership transitions with comparative context about global norms and institutional factors rather than national devourment metaphor.
biases.example_text: Why Britain devours its prime ministers
biases.unbiased_text: Britain has experienced frequent changes in prime minister due to factors including weak coalition support, volatile public opinion, and internal party divisions.

biases.detail: Framing anticorruption efforts through skeptical 'but is it enough?' questioning that positions reforms as inherently insufficient before evaluating their actual scope or impact.
biases.debias: Report anticorruption measures factually with their scale and scope, allowing readers to assess adequacy based on evidence rather than preemptive skepticism.
biases.example_text: Iraq's new PM launches anticorruption campaign, but is it enough? Al-Zaidi campaign to combat corruption seizes $86m, properties, vehicles and gold. But analysts say he needs to do more.
biases.unbiased_text: Iraq's new PM launches anticorruption campaign. Al-Zaidi's campaign to combat corruption has seized $86m, properties, vehicles and gold. Analysts say additional measures may be necessary to address systemic issues.

biases.detail: Framing electoral participation by specific demographic groups as signaling transformative political force rather than reporting election results neutrally.
biases.debias: Report election outcomes and candidate platforms factually without attributing broader movement significance to demographic participation patterns.
biases.example_text: New York's primaries signal a new force in US politics. Progressive, Muslim and Arab American candidates are challenging old limits on debate over Israel and Palestine.
biases.unbiased_text: Muslim and Arab American candidates won several New York Democratic primary races. These candidates have advocated for policy changes regarding Israel and Palestine.

biases.detail: Using 'acting' title in headline when describing government officials responding to crisis implies provisional or illegitimate authority during emergency.
biases.debias: Use official titles without delegitimizing qualifiers unless the acting status is central to the story's focus.
biases.example_text: Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez has been jeered by residents devastated by the earthquakes.
biases.unbiased_text: Venezuela's President Delcy Rodriguez has been jeered by residents devastated by the earthquakes.

biases.detail: Elevating apparent rejection of diplomatic communication channel through scare-quote headline and 'appears to rebuff' language before confirmation.
biases.debias: Report on diplomatic communication mechanisms with confirmed statements rather than apparent rejections.
biases.example_text: 'Pick up the phone': IRGC appears to rebuff US Strait of Hormuz 'hotline'
biases.unbiased_text: IRGC denies existence of US Strait of Hormuz hotline

biases.detail: Framing educational testing through displacement conditions emphasizes ongoing victimization and crisis normalization.
biases.debias: Report on educational continuity efforts without foregrounding displacement as primary context unless examining educational policy.
biases.example_text: No school, living in a tent, but it's exam time in Gaza
biases.unbiased_text: Gaza students take high school exams amid challenging conditions

biases.detail: Using expert interviews or academic voices to elevate specific narratives (like 'genocide' or 'corporate media complicity') to institutional authority status rather than contested viewpoints.
biases.debias: Present expert opinions as perspectives within broader debates, clearly labeling them as analysis rather than established fact.
biases.example_text: Marc Lamont Hill speaks with author Adam Johnson on US corporate media's role in enabling the genocide in Gaza.
biases.unbiased_text: Marc Lamont Hill speaks with author Adam Johnson on his analysis of how US corporate media covered the Gaza conflict.

biases.detail: Framing attacks on agricultural infrastructure as systematic campaigns to dispossess a population rather than military operations with mixed effects.
biases.debias: Report agricultural damage factually while noting military rationales and avoiding deterministic language about intent to dispossess.
biases.example_text: Israel is attacking West Bank agriculture in an attempt to drive Palestinian farmers off their land.
biases.unbiased_text: Israeli military operations in the West Bank have damaged agricultural infrastructure, affecting Palestinian farmers' ability to work their land.

biases.detail: Emphasizing specific time periods for diplomatic actions (like '30 days' of control) to create urgency and frame negotiating positions as temporary concessions.
biases.debias: Report time-limited arrangements factually without implying urgency or casting temporary measures as concessions.
biases.example_text: Iran's foreign minister has urged 'all parties not to interfere' in the management of the Strait of Hormuz.
biases.unbiased_text: Iran's foreign minister stated that the Strait of Hormuz will remain under Iranian management during the current negotiating period.

biases.detail: Framing current political actions as calculated moves for future electoral campaigns rather than policy positions.
biases.debias: Report political decisions and statements on their merits without speculating about future campaign motivations.
biases.example_text: The vice president's decision to criticise Israel and distance himself from rival Rubio means he is reading the base.
biases.unbiased_text: The vice president has criticised Israel and taken positions that differ from those of Secretary of State Rubio.

biases.detail: Using question headlines to imply policy failure or ineffectiveness without making direct assertions.
biases.debias: State facts about policy outcomes directly rather than framing them as open questions implying failure.
biases.example_text: Why Pakistan's Afghan air strikes aren't stopping armed attacks
biases.unbiased_text: Pakistan continues air strikes in Afghanistan as armed attacks persist

biases.detail: Elevating minor viral social media incidents as expressions of national or ideological solidarity movements.
biases.debias: Report viral incidents proportionally without amplifying them as representative of broader political sentiment.
biases.example_text: A video of an Israeli flag being grabbed off two young men in Indonesia has gone viral.
biases.unbiased_text: A video showing Brazil supporters removing an Israeli flag from motorcyclists in Indonesia has circulated on social media.

biases.pattern: Bilateral debt relief strategic benefit insinuation
biases.detail: Framing debt forgiveness as transactional moves that benefit the creditor nation rather than humanitarian gestures.
biases.debias: Report debt relief agreements factually, noting stated purposes without speculating on hidden strategic motives.
biases.example_text: China and Sudan signed off on a waiver of $50m as Sudan's military-led government seeks support amid Western sanctions.
biases.unbiased_text: China waived $50 million in loans to Sudan. Sudan's government has been under Western sanctions.

biases.detail: Presenting official resignations after failures as proof of systemic accountability demands rather than routine consequences.
biases.debias: Report resignations as administrative changes without framing them as validation of protest or criticism movements.
biases.example_text: Saudi Arabia's early FIFA World Cup exit prompts federation chief to resign
biases.unbiased_text: Saudi Arabia's football federation chief resigned after the team's early World Cup exit.

biases.detail: Characterizing diplomatic agreements as one party's capitulation to another's demands rather than mutual negotiations.
biases.debias: Present diplomatic agreements as negotiations between parties rather than unilateral victories or surrenders.
biases.example_text: President Zelenskyy demands Lukashenko shut down stations installed by Russia 'or we will'.
biases.unbiased_text: Ukraine and Belarus reached an agreement regarding stations near their border.

biases.detail: Framing corporate data breaches as revelatory leaks of consumer-relevant secrets rather than security incidents affecting business operations.
biases.debias: Report data breaches as security incidents with business impact context, not as consumer product revelation opportunities.
biases.example_text: Apple iPhone 18 Pro secrets leaked in Tata Electronics hack: What we know
biases.unbiased_text: Tata Electronics suffers data breach affecting Apple supplier operations

biases.detail: Highlighting religious or cultural venues hosting World Cup watch parties to emphasize community identity and belonging narratives.
biases.debias: Report watch party locations neutrally without emphasizing identity-based community gathering as notable.
biases.example_text: At an Islamic centre in US, World Cup watch parties are giving many a place to cheer on teams chasing football history.
biases.unbiased_text: World Cup fans gather at community venues across the US to watch matches.

biases.detail: Elevating routine post-victory family celebrations into emotionally significant moments worthy of separate coverage.
biases.debias: Include family celebrations as normal post-match details without separate amplification as newsworthy events.
biases.example_text: Morocco's Ismael Saibari embraced his mother after scoring the winning penalty against Netherlands.
biases.unbiased_text: Morocco defeated the Netherlands on penalties, with Ismael Saibari scoring the decisive kick.

biases.detail: Presenting judicial rulings as scoreboard victories or defeats for political leaders rather than legal determinations.
biases.debias: Report court rulings by their legal substance and implications, not as political win-loss records.
biases.example_text: US Supreme Court hands Trump 3-1 defeat in key rulings: What we know
biases.unbiased_text: US Supreme Court issues rulings on mail-in ballots, the E Jean Carroll case, and the firing of Lisa Cook

biases.detail: Headlines about Afghanistan firing drones into Pakistan omit context of prior Pakistani strikes, presenting only the Afghan action as newsworthy aggression.
biases.debias: Include full context of reciprocal cross-border strikes when framing drone attacks between neighboring states.
biases.example_text: After Afghanistan fires drones into Pakistan, what's next?
biases.unbiased_text: After latest exchange of cross-border strikes between Afghanistan and Pakistan, what's next?

biases.detail: Frames Europe as caught or trapped between US and China, portraying external powers as the source of European economic challenges rather than internal policy choices.
biases.debias: Present Europe's trade relationships as strategic choices rather than passive victimization by larger powers.
biases.example_text: Caught between the US and China, can Europe remain competitive?
biases.unbiased_text: As Europe navigates relations with the US and China, can it remain competitive?

biases.detail: Emphasizes that incumbent has been in office for the entire lifetime of younger challenger, framing longevity as inherently problematic rather than experienced.
biases.debias: Report electoral victories based on policy platforms and voter preferences rather than age-based tenure comparisons.
biases.example_text: Melat Kiros defeated Diana DeGette, who has been in office for as long as the 29-year-old Kiros has been alive.
biases.unbiased_text: Melat Kiros, 29, defeated incumbent Diana DeGette in the primary election.

biases.detail: Headlines nationality and business status of bombing victim before establishing facts, creating narrative frame around who rather than what occurred. Also: Identifying bombing victims prominently by their tycoon status rather than their names or citizenship, emphasizing wealth over personhood in attack narratives.
biases.debias: Lead with incident details before victim identity to avoid implying motive or significance through selective identification. Identify attack victims by name and citizenship first, mentioning business status as secondary context if relevant.
biases.example_text: Who is Vadym Yermolaiev, the Ukrainian tycoon injured in Monaco blast?
biases.unbiased_text: Explosive device injures businessman in Monaco; police search for suspect

biases.pattern: Mental health harm scam victimization universalization
biases.detail: Headlines mental health impacts of scams using majority framing to universalize psychological vulnerability and emphasize societal crisis dimension.
biases.debias: Report scam statistics including mental health impacts without using majority framing that implies universal vulnerability.
biases.example_text: Nearly three in four US scam victims report mental health harm, poll finds
biases.unbiased_text: US scam victims reported $68bn in losses in 2025, with many experiencing mental health impacts, poll finds

biases.detail: Emphasizes diaspora presence and political solidarity at sporting events, framing tournament as platform for national identity rather than athletic competition.
biases.debias: Report on sporting events primarily through athletic performance while noting fan presence without political identity emphasis.
biases.example_text: Tournament has placed Bosnia's fans and global diaspora in the spotlight, as team fights to reach Round of 16.
biases.unbiased_text: Bosnia's national team advances in tournament as fans travel to support them in reaching the Round of 16.

biases.detail: Framing the reopening of supply routes as potentially creating the opposite problem (surplus/glut) rather than stability restoration.
biases.debias: Report supply route restoration as normalization without speculating on overcorrection scenarios.
biases.example_text: With Hormuz reopened, has the oil shortage turned into a glut? As flow resumes through the strait, an oil surplus may yet again destabilise global energy markets.
biases.unbiased_text: With Hormuz reopened, oil flow through the strait resumes. Market analysts are monitoring supply levels as shipping returns to normal.

biases.detail: Framing amputee athletic participation as reclaiming space that war 'tried to take' rather than adaptive sports development.
biases.debias: Report amputee sports programs as adaptive athletics without metaphors of territorial reclamation from conflict.
biases.example_text: Gaza's first women's amputee football team is reclaiming a space that war tried to take from them.
biases.unbiased_text: Gaza's first women's amputee football team has formed and is practicing.

biases.detail: Leading with percentage-based destruction and seizure statistics to emphasize scale through numerical framing.
biases.debias: Report damage assessments without leading headlines with percentage figures as primary framing.
biases.example_text: Gaza war's 1,000 days: 90% of strip 'destroyed', 80% 'seized' by Israel
biases.unbiased_text: Gaza war reaches 1,000 days with extensive damage and territorial control changes documented.

biases.detail: Drawing historical parallels between current coaching criticism and past discrimination cases to suggest ethnic targeting pattern.
biases.debias: Report coaching controversies on their specific merits without importing historical discrimination analogies.
biases.example_text: Eight years ago, it was Mesut Ozil, who has Turkish roots. This time, German manager tries to blame Kurdish Deniz Undav.
biases.unbiased_text: German manager's criticism of player Deniz Undav after World Cup loss has sparked debate about team dynamics.

biases.detail: Characterizing new legislation as potentially hastening forced assimilation and targeting critics without presenting government justification.
biases.debias: Report legislation provisions with both government rationale and critic concerns in balanced proportion.
biases.example_text: Critics say it could hasten forced assimilation, lead to targeting of critics outside China. Beijing rejects charges.
biases.unbiased_text: China's new ethnic unity law has been criticized by some groups as potentially affecting minority practices, while the government says it promotes social cohesion.

biases.detail: Highlighting and celebrating an athlete's use of Islamic invocations as culturally significant moments worthy of amplification and positive framing.
biases.debias: Report religious expressions by athletes neutrally without celebratory emphasis or cultural validation framing.
biases.example_text: Cristiano Ronaldo appeared to say 'Bismillah' (In the name of God) twice before taking a penalty.
biases.unbiased_text: Cristiano Ronaldo was observed saying words before taking a penalty kick during the match.

biases.detail: Framing volunteer emergency services through a questioning lens that presents their work as potentially dangerous rather than beneficial, emphasizing risk over service.
biases.debias: Report on volunteer emergency services by describing their functions and challenges without paradoxical questioning of their value.
biases.example_text: Bangkok's ambulance volunteers: Saving lives or putting them at risk?
biases.unbiased_text: Bangkok's volunteer ambulance crews face challenges and risks as they respond to accident scenes across the city.

biases.detail: Framing routine security interactions between police and athletes as confrontational altercations, emphasizing conflict over standard procedures.
biases.debias: Report security interactions with sports teams by describing what occurred without characterizing routine procedures as confrontations.
biases.example_text: US Police staff spark altercation with Egyptian players posing with fans
biases.unbiased_text: US police intervened as Egyptian national team players posed with fans at their Dallas hotel.

biases.detail: Emphasizing altitude's physical challenges as a disadvantage narrative for visiting teams in sports coverage.
biases.debias: Report altitude as a neutral geographic fact without framing it as primarily a hardship or disadvantage.
biases.example_text: The pitch at the Azteca is 2,240 metres above sea level. At that altitude, air is thinner and makes breathing difficult.
biases.unbiased_text: The pitch at the Azteca is 2,240 metres above sea level, where atmospheric pressure is lower than at sea level.

biases.detail: Framing shifts in bilateral relations as one nation 'no longer asking permission' to suggest hierarchy reversal.
biases.debias: Describe policy changes in neutral terms without implying subordination metaphors.
biases.example_text: Washington has started dealing with regional players without regard for Indian interests.
biases.unbiased_text: Washington has shifted its approach to regional engagement, pursuing direct bilateral relationships.

biases.detail: Presenting celebrity marriages as major news events with venue and guest emphasis suggesting broader significance.
biases.debias: Report celebrity personal events in entertainment sections without elevating to news headline priority.
biases.example_text: A-list celebrities attend wedding at Madison Square Garden to see superstar couple tie the knot.
biases.unbiased_text: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce were married in a private ceremony in New York City.

biases.detail: Highlighting age-based athletic records as standalone achievements without contextualizing performance outcomes or competitive merit.
biases.debias: Report age records alongside match results and performance context to avoid treating youth itself as the primary achievement.
biases.example_text: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest debutant for India in a T20 loss to England at Old Trafford.
biases.unbiased_text: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, made his debut for India in a T20 match against England at Old Trafford, which India lost.

biases.detail: Amplifying promises of preferential treatment to 'friendly' nations as diplomatic victories while omitting implications for international norms.
biases.debias: Report diplomatic assurances while noting potential conflicts with international law or equal treatment principles.
biases.example_text: Despite US objections, ambassador insists new fees to be charged to vessels transiting Strait of Hormuz.
biases.unbiased_text: Iran's ambassador to China stated that new fees will be charged for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, a policy the US has objected to.

biases.detail: Framing release of detained religious figures as victories for religious freedom while omitting ongoing restrictions on religious practice.
biases.debias: Report releases factually while providing context about broader religious freedom conditions and legal frameworks.
biases.example_text: Ezra Jin's family says the Zion Church founder arrived in the US after months in detention in China.
biases.unbiased_text: Ezra Jin, founder of Zion Church, arrived in the US following his detention in China, according to his family.

biases.detail: Attributing infant death causally to military checkpoint obstruction without medical verification of alternative outcome.
biases.debias: Report checkpoint delay factually while noting medical cause of death remains undetermined by authorities.
biases.example_text: A baby died after his family's attempt to reach hospital was blocked by Israel at a checkpoint in the occupied West Bank
biases.unbiased_text: A baby died after his family reported being delayed at an Israeli checkpoint in the occupied West Bank while attempting to reach hospital.

biases.detail: Framing dissolution of militant governance as automatic pathway to legitimate civilian administration.
biases.debias: Note governance transition announcement while acknowledging implementation challenges and legitimacy questions remain unresolved.
biases.example_text: A Palestinian technocratic committee will take its place to manage the enclave's day-to-day governance.
biases.unbiased_text: Hamas announced a Palestinian technocratic committee would be established to manage the enclave's day-to-day governance, though implementation details remain unclear.

biases.detail: Emphasizing that two mothers both believe the same bound detainee image shows their missing son to amplify the tragedy and confusion of occupation.
biases.debias: Report the factual situation without dramatizing the emotional conflict of competing maternal claims.
biases.example_text: Two Palestinian mothers believe a viral image of a bound Gaza detainee shows their missing son.
biases.unbiased_text: A viral image of a bound Gaza detainee has led to conflicting claims about the person's identity.

biases.detail: Framing a coach's pre-match statement as an impassioned plea for Palestine to merge sports coverage with political advocacy.
biases.debias: Report coach statements without characterizing political commentary as passionate advocacy.
biases.example_text: Egypt coach makes impassioned plea for Palestine in pre-match conference
biases.unbiased_text: Egypt coach commented on Palestine during pre-match press conference.

biases.detail: Presents global mortality record-keeping as fundamentally broken through rhetorical questioning, implying systemic failure rather than methodological challenges.
biases.debias: Present mortality data collection challenges as technical issues being addressed rather than existential crises of knowledge.
biases.example_text: Why can't we count our dead? Most of the world's dead never make the official record. The death toll is an educated guess, not an actual count.
biases.unbiased_text: Global mortality tracking faces data collection challenges in many regions. Official death tolls often rely on statistical modeling in areas with limited vital registration systems.

biases.pattern: Joke candidate legitimization through headline parity
biases.detail: Presenting satirical or novelty political candidates in headlines with the same structural format as serious candidates, implicitly elevating their legitimacy.
biases.debias: Clearly identify satirical candidates as such in headlines and ledes, distinguishing them from serious political contenders.
biases.example_text: 'Not Nigel Farage': Who is Count Binface, contesting as MP for Clacton, UK?
biases.unbiased_text: Count Binface, a comedic performance art candidate known for wearing a bin-shaped helmet, is running against Nigel Farage in Clacton.

biases.detail: Highlighting difficult environmental conditions during mass gatherings to amplify narrative of devotion or sacrifice by participants.
biases.debias: Report weather conditions factually without using them to characterize participant motivation or dedication.
biases.example_text: Iranians gather in sweltering heat for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's funeral in his hometown of Mashhad.
biases.unbiased_text: Iranians gather for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's funeral in his hometown of Mashhad, where temperatures reached high levels.

biases.detail: Natural disasters are framed with geographic comparisons to Western countries to dramatize scale for international audiences.
biases.debias: Report the actual measurements and affected area without comparative geographic framing.
biases.example_text: As Super Typhoon Bavi approaches, residents in Taiwan, Japan and China have been stockpiling supplies.
biases.unbiased_text: Super Typhoon Bavi is approaching Taiwan, Japan and China, prompting residents to stockpile supplies.

biases.detail: Incarceration conditions are characterized as a form of death itself rather than describing specific harms.
biases.debias: Report documented harms and conditions without metaphorical death equivalences.
biases.example_text: A firsthand account shows how isolation and neglect can make incarceration a slow form of death in U.S. prisons.
biases.unbiased_text: A firsthand account describes conditions of isolation and neglect in a U.S. prison.

biases.detail: Elections after long gaps are framed as democratic breakthroughs without questioning underlying constraints.
biases.debias: Report election announcements while noting continuing restrictions on sovereignty or governance.
biases.example_text: First Palestinian legislative elections in 20 years announced
biases.unbiased_text: Palestinian legislative elections have been announced for the first time since 2006.

biases.detail: Framing power outages as primarily affecting hospitals and medical care to amplify humanitarian crisis narrative rather than broader infrastructure impact.
biases.debias: Report power outages with proportional coverage of all affected sectors including healthcare, residential, and commercial infrastructure.
biases.example_text: Gaza is suffering from an energy crisis, affecting hospitals struggling to treat patients amid Israeli bombing.
biases.unbiased_text: Gaza is experiencing power outages affecting multiple sectors including hospitals, residential areas, and infrastructure amid ongoing conflict.

biases.detail: Highlighting specific nationality of disaster victims to create international incident framing rather than reporting casualties neutrally.
biases.debias: Report disaster casualties with factual numbers without emphasizing victim nationalities unless directly relevant to diplomatic response.
biases.example_text: Speedboat accident in southern Vietnam kills 15 Indian tourists
biases.unbiased_text: Speedboat accident in southern Vietnam kills 15 people

biases.detail: Using the honorific 'Father Emir' repeatedly in headlines and text frames the deceased ruler as a paternal national figure rather than a political leader.
biases.debias: Use the leader's official title without familial framing that implies a paternalistic relationship with citizens.
biases.example_text: Qatar mourns Father Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani
biases.unbiased_text: Qatar mourns former Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani

biases.detail: Attributing a prominent political figure's death to unspecified 'sudden illness' without medical details creates narrative ambiguity that can fuel speculation.
biases.debias: Report available medical information or acknowledge when details are not disclosed, without using vague terms that suggest mystery.
biases.example_text: The US Republican senator died of a sudden illness, his office said. He was 71.
biases.unbiased_text: The US Republican senator died at age 71, according to his office, which did not immediately disclose the cause of death.

biases.detail: Framing articles as neutral 'explainers' while embedding advocacy positions through selective emphasis on illegality and policy advocacy.
biases.debias: Recognize that explainer formats can embed bias through question framing and answer structure; ensure balanced presentation of competing legal and policy perspectives.
biases.example_text: What is the EU's plan to cut trade with illegal Israeli settlements? Foreign ministers' meeting comes months after the EU imposed sanctions on Israel over West Bank settlement construction.
biases.unbiased_text: What is the EU's plan regarding trade with Israeli settlements? Foreign ministers meet to discuss proposals, months after the EU imposed sanctions on Israel over West Bank settlement construction.

biases.detail: Framing a new policy as a 'reinstatement' implies it existed before and is merely being restored, rather than presenting it as a new action or escalation.
biases.debias: State the action as new policy implementation without implying prior legitimacy through 'reinstatement' framing.
biases.example_text: US President Donald Trump says he is reinstating a blockade on Iran in the Strait of Hormuz
biases.unbiased_text: US President Donald Trump says he is imposing a blockade on Iran in the Strait of Hormuz

biases.detail: Elevating a government's filing of criminal complaints to headline status frames a diplomatic dispute as a matter of criminal justice, strengthening the accusatory narrative.
biases.debias: Report diplomatic or legal actions neutrally without criminal justice framing that prejudges outcomes.
biases.example_text: Mexico files criminal complaints over migrant deaths during ICE operations
biases.unbiased_text: Mexico formally protests migrant deaths during ICE operations

biases.detail: Frames hereditary political succession as automatic institutional process without highlighting its departure from democratic norms.
biases.debias: Explicitly identify hereditary political succession as exceptional and contrast with standard democratic selection processes.
biases.example_text: The late senator's sister, the politically inexperienced Darline Graham Nordone, has inherited his office and powers.
biases.unbiased_text: The late senator's sister, the politically inexperienced Darline Graham Nordone, has been appointed to temporarily fill his office under South Carolina's unusual hereditary succession law, which differs from the standard democratic practice of special elections or gubernatorial appointments of qualified candidates.

biases.detail: Attributes national economic crisis exclusively to foreign policy threats rather than acknowledging multiple contributing factors.
biases.debias: Present foreign policy actions as one factor among multiple structural and historical causes of economic conditions.
biases.example_text: Fuel has been scarce across Cuba since January, when US President Donald Trump threatened to impose tariffs on any nation that supplies or sells oil to the island, exacerbating the island's continuing financial and economic crises.
biases.unbiased_text: Fuel has been scarce across Cuba since January, when US President Donald Trump threatened to impose tariffs on any nation that supplies or sells oil to the island. Cuba has faced continuing financial and economic crises due to multiple factors including infrastructure deterioration, existing US sanctions, and limited access to international credit.

biases.detail: Emphasizing a scholar's role in building connections between cultures/religions as their primary achievement amplifies interfaith harmony narratives.
biases.debias: Report scholarly contributions objectively without framing their work primarily through a bridge-building lens.
biases.example_text: Georgetown scholar and author spent decades building bridges between the Islamic and Western worlds.
biases.unbiased_text: Georgetown scholar and author specialized in Islamic studies and interfaith relations for decades.

biases.detail: Using scare quotes around 'far-left political violence and terrorism' questions the validity of the threat designation while reporting on official security conferences.
biases.debias: Report the conference subject matter directly without using scare quotes that editorialize the threat assessment.
biases.example_text: More than 65 countries expected to address 'renewed threats' from 'far-left political violence and terrorism'.
biases.unbiased_text: More than 65 countries expected to address renewed threats from far-left political violence and terrorism.

biases.detail: Presenting government programs to separate family members from organized crime as humanitarian rescue operations rather than coercive law enforcement measures.
biases.debias: Report such programs neutrally by noting both stated aims and civil liberties concerns about family separation policies.
biases.example_text: The Italian government can now offer children and wives of mafia bosses a way out of the family business.
biases.unbiased_text: Italy has enacted legislation allowing authorities to separate children and spouses from suspected mafia members, which supporters say protects vulnerable family members while critics raise concerns about due process.

biases.detail: Characterizing legal action against political donors as intimidation campaigns targeting broader activist communities rather than individual criminal cases.
biases.debias: Report prosecutions by stating charges and evidence while avoiding implications that cases are designed to deter entire political movements.
biases.example_text: Washington's pursuit of James 'Fergie' Chambers for supporting 'terror' seen as a warning to other left-leaning donors.
biases.unbiased_text: The US is seeking extradition of donor James Chambers from Spain on charges related to material support for designated terrorist organizations.

biases.detail: Updating death tolls progressively in separate articles creates serialized tragedy narrative rather than single complete report.
biases.debias: Report final confirmed casualty figures in comprehensive single updates rather than incremental serialization.
biases.example_text: Three more pupils died after Uganda's school bus crash, raising the death toll to 23 students and one adult.
biases.unbiased_text: A school bus crash in Uganda killed 23 students and one adult, authorities confirmed.

biases.detail: Framing diaspora fan communities as preserving national tradition emphasizes cultural continuity over sporting interest.
biases.debias: Report fan enthusiasm without cultural preservation framing.
biases.example_text: Argentinians in Queens hold on to football tradition, as new communities grow support the national team in NYC.
biases.unbiased_text: Argentinians in Queens support their national team ahead of the World Cup final in NYC.

biases.detail: Portraying entire cities or regions as unified behind single athlete creates monolithic support narrative.
biases.debias: Report fan enthusiasm without claiming universal city-wide unity.
biases.example_text: South Asia's greatest football city has united behind its footballing saint.
biases.unbiased_text: Many football fans in Kolkata support Messi ahead of the World Cup final.

biases.detail: Characterizing medical intervention for a hunger-striking activist as 'illegal detention' or 'enforced hospitalization' rather than emergency medical care.
biases.debias: Report medical intervention for hunger strikers as health-protective measures while noting the activist's stated objections, without prejudging legality.
biases.example_text: The wife of 59-year-old Sonam Wangchuk says his enforced hospitalisation is 'illegal detention'.
biases.unbiased_text: The wife of 59-year-old Sonam Wangchuk says his hospitalization against his wishes violates his rights, though a court has rejected the release petition.

biases.detail: Framing sports team support as evidence of political solidarity with a cause or nation, conflating athletic preference with political alignment.
biases.debias: Report sports preferences as entertainment choices while noting any political statements made separately by fans, without presuming political motivation.
biases.example_text: Football fans in Gaza express support for Spain in showdown with Argentina, citing Spanish solidarity with Palestinians.
biases.unbiased_text: Football fans in Gaza are supporting Spain in the World Cup final, with some citing Spain's political stance on Palestinian issues as a factor in their preference.

biases.detail: Framing government review of library materials as 'vetting' or searching for 'objectionable' content, implying censorship without examining stated justifications.
biases.debias: Report library reviews with specific details about stated rationales, scope, and outcomes, allowing readers to assess the nature of the policy.
biases.example_text: Authorities in disputed region are auditing school, college and public libraries to look for 'objectionable' material.
biases.unbiased_text: Authorities in the region are reviewing library collections, stating they are checking for material they define as promoting separatism or violence against the state.

biases.detail: Combining an outgoing leader's farewell address with calls for protests in the headline, suggesting the speech itself is about disputing results rather than a traditional departure message.
biases.debias: Separate ceremonial farewell speeches from electoral dispute activities to avoid conflating standard political transitions with resistance movements.
biases.example_text: The outgoing president has called for protests as he continues to dispute the results of last month's election.
biases.unbiased_text: The outgoing president will give a farewell speech. He has separately called for protests and disputed last month's election results.

biases.detail: Attributing a population's support for a sports team primarily to that team's government's political positions rather than traditional sporting loyalty or other cultural factors.
biases.debias: Acknowledge multiple reasons people support sports teams, including national pride, playing style, and individual athletes, rather than reducing it to political alignment.
biases.example_text: Thousands gathered across Gaza to watch the World Cup final, with many backing Spain over its support for Palestinians.
biases.unbiased_text: Thousands gathered across Gaza to watch the World Cup final, with many supporting Spain.

biases.detail: Suggesting that a sports victory brings joy specifically to critics of certain countries based on the winning nation's diplomatic positions, politicizing athletic achievement.
biases.debias: Report on sports victories as primarily athletic accomplishments, noting diplomatic context separately without suggesting the victory itself validates political positions.
biases.example_text: Iran says Spain World Cup win brings joy to critics of US, Israel
biases.unbiased_text: Iran's officials commented on Spain's World Cup win, noting Spain's diplomatic positions on Gaza and Iran policy.

biases.detail: Using quotation marks around 'ceasefire' while simultaneously noting ongoing attacks emphasizes the illegitimacy of peace agreements through temporal contradiction.
biases.debias: Report violations of agreements without delegitimizing the agreements themselves through punctuation.
biases.example_text: Israeli forces launch regular attacks on Gaza despite a US-backed 'ceasefire' agreed in October.
biases.unbiased_text: Israeli forces launch regular attacks on Gaza despite a US-backed ceasefire agreed in October.

biases.detail: Using derogatory nicknames for protest movements (e.g., 'cockroach protest movement') in headlines reinforces stigmatizing labels.
biases.debias: Refer to protest movements by their formal names or descriptive identifiers without using stigmatizing nicknames.
biases.example_text: India's 'cockroach' protest movement halts marches after police violence
biases.unbiased_text: India's student protest movement halts marches after police violence

biases.detail: Emphasizing that victims were burned so severely they became unrecognizable serves to amplify horror and suffering rather than report death neutrally.
biases.debias: Report casualties and manner of death factually without emphasizing degradation of remains.
biases.example_text: An Israeli strike hit a civilian vehicle in central Gaza, killing two Palestinians burnt beyond recognition
biases.unbiased_text: An Israeli strike hit a civilian vehicle in central Gaza, killing two Palestinians.

biases.detail: Presenting non-Western cultural practices as quirky curiosities through headline emphasis on unusual prizes trivializes local traditions as entertainment.
biases.debias: Report cultural practices neutrally without emphasizing novelty or framing them as exotic spectacles.
biases.example_text: GOATs are not players, but prizes at this football tournament in eastern India.
biases.unbiased_text: A football tournament in eastern India awards livestock as prizes, continuing a longstanding local tradition.

biases.detail: Appending '-gate' suffix to allegations elevates them to the level of major political scandals before full adjudication.
biases.debias: Describe allegations factually without using scandal-implying terminology that presumes significance.
biases.example_text: Allegations of spying on rivals led to Southampton's expulsion from the Championship playoff final.
biases.unbiased_text: Allegations of scouting violations led to Southampton's expulsion from the Championship playoff final.

biases.detail: Assigning evocative names to military demarcation lines frames them as deliberate tools of territorial seizure rather than tactical boundaries.
biases.debias: Describe military boundaries by their function without metaphorical names that presume annexation intent.
biases.example_text: 'Creeping death': Israel weaponises 'Yellow Line' to annex Gaza
biases.unbiased_text: Israel establishes buffer zone in Gaza as analysts debate its implications for territorial control

biases.detail: Converting local purchasing power into Big Mac meals to dramatize economic inequality between cities.
biases.debias: Report actual wage data and cost-of-living metrics without novelty food comparisons.
biases.example_text: A worker in Cairo can afford 22 hamburgers a month. In Tel Aviv, more than 200. AJLabs counts a salary in Big Mac meals.
biases.unbiased_text: Workers in Cairo earn significantly less in purchasing power terms than workers in Tel Aviv, according to cost-of-living comparisons.

biases.detail: Emphasizing ongoing legal restrictions immediately after reporting someone's release to undermine the significance of their freedom.
biases.debias: Report release first as primary news, then note any continuing legal obligations separately.
biases.example_text: Indian authorities release the two men after years in prison although both remain under tight court-imposed restrictions
biases.unbiased_text: Indian authorities released the two men after years in prison on bail, subject to court-imposed conditions.

biases.detail: Using multiplication factors to emphasize reconstruction costs by comparing to previous conflicts.
biases.debias: Report absolute costs and timelines without dramatic multiplier comparisons.
biases.example_text: Rebuilding the enclave will cost seven times the combined cost of all past offensives, says joint report.
biases.unbiased_text: Rebuilding the enclave will cost $71 billion, according to a joint report.

biases.unbiased_text: Analysts at major banks project the Iran conflict will shift oil markets into a supply deficit for 2026
